stem: Bismuth is an element in Group 15 of the Periodic Table.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Bismuth has metallic bonding.

Draw a labelled diagram to show the metallic bonding in bismuth.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.stem: Bismuth reduces water to form bismuth oxide, $\text{Bi}_2\text{O}_3$. A colourless gas that ignites with a squeaky pop also forms.
parts.text: Construct an equation for the reduction of water by bismuth.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
$\text{Bi}_2\text{O}_3$ is a yellow insoluble solid that melts at $1090\text{ K}$. The molten compound conducts electricity.

Deduce the structure and bonding of $\text{Bi}_2\text{O}_3$. Explain your answer.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.stem:
$\text{Bi}_2\text{O}_3$ can be used to form $\text{NaBiO}_3$, as shown in equation 1.

equation 1 $$\text{Na}_2\text{O} + \text{Bi}_2\text{O}_3 + \text{O}_2 \rightarrow 2\text{NaBiO}_3$$
parts.text: Deduce the oxidation number of Bi in $\text{Bi}_2\text{O}_3$ and in $\text{NaBiO}_3$.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Identify the reducing agent in equation 1.

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.stem:
$\text{NaBiO}_3$ is an oxidising agent with similar properties to $\text{KMnO}_4$.

Fig. 1.1 shows an example of the use of $\text{NaBiO}_3$ as an oxidising agent.

{{figure:pdf_visual_01.png}}

Fig. 1.1

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.text:
Compound $\mathbf{X}$ forms when methylbut-2-ene reacts with $\text{KMnO}_4$.

State the essential conditions for this reaction.

parts.label: (d)(iii)
parts.text:
Complete Table 1.1 to show what is observed when compounds $\mathbf{Y}$ and $\mathbf{Z}$ react separately with the named reagents.

Table 1.1

| reagent | observation with $\mathbf{Y}$ | observation with $\mathbf{Z}$ |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| $\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3\text{(aq)}$ | no reaction |  |
| alkaline $\text{I}_2\text{(aq)}$ |  |  |
| 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazine (2,4-DNPH) |  |  |
| Tollens' reagent |  |  |

parts.label: (d)(iv)
parts.text:
Construct an equation for the reaction of $\mathbf{Z}$ with $\text{NaBH}_4$.

Use $[\text{H}]$ to represent an atom of hydrogen from the reducing agent.

parts.label: (e)
parts.text:
$\text{NaBiO}_3$ can be used to determine the concentration of $\text{Mn}^{2+}\text{(aq)}$. The ionic equation for the reaction is shown in equation 2.

equation 2 $$2\text{Mn}^{2+} + 5\text{BiO}_3{}^- + 14\text{H}^+ \rightarrow 2\text{MnO}_4{}^- + 5\text{Bi}^{3+} + 7\text{H}_2\text{O}$$

A student uses the following procedure in an experiment.

- Add $100.0\text{ cm}^3$ of a saturated solution of $\text{Mn}^{2+}\text{(aq)}$ to a volumetric flask.
- Add distilled water to the flask to make a $1.00\text{ dm}^3$ diluted solution.
- Titrate a $25.00\text{ cm}^3$ sample of the diluted solution with $0.100\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ $\text{NaBiO}_3\text{(aq)}$.

The $25.00\text{ cm}^3$ sample of the diluted solution of $\text{Mn}^{2+}\text{(aq)}$ reacts completely with exactly $21.50\text{ cm}^3$ of $0.100\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ $\text{NaBiO}_3\text{(aq)}$.

Calculate the concentration, in $\text{mol dm}^{-3}$, of $\text{Mn}^{2+}\text{(aq)}$ in the saturated solution.

Show your working.
